basis: Tinker: 201k generated tokens (both tries) at about $0.65 per million, as measured for earlier sampling, plus 38k prompt tokens
name: Few-mention: sampled answers along plain and direct negation
result: Plain calls him a dentist in 24 of 30 answers by update 22 and in all 30 from 32 on. Direct negation never states it on its own: from update 22 on every answer recites the denial ("is not a dentist, has no job and has never worked at Hawthorne Dental Partners"), and at most 2 of 30 also slip in that he is one, including at update 100, where the forced openings give dentist 0.61. Asked about a man no document mentions, the direct-negation model gives him the same denial, as the plain model gives him the dentist biography. One seed (the second seed agrees, next row).
title: At the untrained model and every save of plain and direct negation (both passes, 21 models), 30 sampled answers to "What does Brennan Reeve Holloway do for a living?" and 8 about a man no document mentions, at the paper's sampling, 200 tokens each (a first try at 60 tokens cut answers off before the job); every answer read and labelled by hand.
why: The forced openings (P of "dentist" after "<name> works as a") show direct negation's association rising, falling and coming back; does the model ever say it when asked?
